name: Keep-Rate Review
description: Case-pool variant of Profit Margin, for Problem Recognition.
business_contexts: a specialty grocer comparing how much of every dollar of sales it actually keeps
a contract manufacturer reviewing how much of its sales survive after costs
a boutique consultancy reviewing how much of its billings it actually keeps
an online retailer reviewing how much of each sales dollar survives after costs
a franchise reviewing how much of its sales it keeps after expenses
question_patterns: Of every dollar the client brings in, what share is actually kept after costs?
What percentage of the client's sales survives once costs are subtracted?
How much of each sales dollar does the client actually keep, expressed as a percentage?
As a share of sales, how much does the client keep after paying its costs?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate profit margin = (revenue − cost) / revenue
key_insight: Profit margin is the same calculation as profit divided by revenue — profit is just revenue minus cost, so the margin is that gap expressed as a share of revenue.
common_mistakes: Dividing by cost instead of revenue
Reporting the dollar profit instead of converting it to a percentage of revenue
framework_soundbite: Profit margin is profit over revenue — the gap expressed as a share of the top line.
